## Provenance

- Corpus: `corpus.py` at this commit: 486 cases, 1603 APDUs per device, in two sessions (settings as
  installed; then "Blind signing" and "Expert mode" switched on through the settings screen).
- C side: v1.3.0 release ELFs from SmartPacts/app-kadena "Reusable build" run 36165620661 (main, 144b30fe),
  artifact `compiled_app_binaries`.
- Rust side: ELFs built with `cargo ledger build` in
  `ghcr.io/ledgerhq/ledger-app-builder/ledger-app-dev-tools@sha256:1f93ba59ee02576f336653c712276f006d4d81f4e355b023489bb7b5bdcf390d`
  (Speculos 0.27.0, Ragger 1.47.3 navigation), seed `equip will roof matter pink blind book anxiety banner elbow sun young`.

Rebuilding the final commit from a fresh clone, mounted at `/app` as here, gives byte-identical ELFs (same sha256
on all five devices). The checkout path is an input: panic locations embed source paths, so a build from another
directory differs.

How the results were collected (at most two emulators at a time):

- Rust side: every case on every device, in one run per device (2026-10-03, the ELFs above, one emulator at a
  time). On Flex, "legacy blob length 205 (device signer)" and "... 206 ..." were run again on their own
  because the full run had not recorded the CAUTION page; their responses were the same in both runs.
- C side: the C binaries never change, so their results are reused. Nano S+ and Nano X: every case of the
  previous corpus in one run per device (2026-09-30). Stax, Flex and Apex P: 408 cases run on 2026-09-29 and 14
  added on 2026-09-30 (on Stax, "legacy blob length 217 (device signer)" was run again on its own because the
  first run had not recorded the CAUTION page the C app shows there). Then, on every device, the retired case
  "V17 other module capability" was dropped and 17 cases were run on 2026-09-30 and merged in: the 14 new ones
  (V20 `coin.DEBIT` / `coin.CREDIT` and another module's capability, V21 with its control, the fractional gas
  limit, V22) and the three "V3 signer" cases, re-run for the new "Key not in transfer" marker. On 2026-10-01
  and 2026-10-02 the 37 round-4 cases (V23 token structured transfers with blind signing ON, the V24 amount
  shapes on 0x22 and 0x03, and the decimal-object controls) were run on every device and merged in, and on
  2026-10-02 the 14 round-5 cases (V25 and V26, the unquoted decimal key, and their controls).

The C fixtures are re-keyed to the test seed's key (V9; `corpus.py` explains how), and the originals are kept
as V9 cases. V9, V11, V12, V14, V18, V20, V22, V24 and V25 are recognised from the input itself and from the C app's
screens (whether it showed a WARNING or CAUTION page), not from the case names, so fuzz cases are classified
the same way. V23 (a token structured transfer: the Rust app needs blind signing) is recognised from the
transfer's namespace and module; V25 and V26 on a structured transfer from its amount field. Since the first
  hardware run an unverified capability is shown as separate items (WARNING "Capability not verified",
  Capability, Namespace when the name has one, Arguments): the cases that show it are V20 or V23 by the
  same rules, the warning marker matching "Capability not verified". The C app shows a decimal-object amount as written and this app shows the
number (V24); the responses are the same.

V7 is checked on the signatures, not only the status words: in "V7 0x02 between INIT and LAST" the Rust
signature verifies under the key of the signing command's path (A) and the C signature under the key of the
path the interleaved 0x02 gave (B).

## Emulator stopped on the C side

Speculos exits (UnicodeDecodeError) when the C app draws bytes that are not UTF-8 on a touch screen; the C response is then unavailable. The Rust app refuses these inputs.
